subject: Materials Science
title: Quantum Confinement
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Quantum Confinement.

hook.text: Quantum dots glow different colors based purely on their size — same material, different diameter, different color.

buildup.text: When a particle shrinks below the exciton Bohr radius, electrons are confined — energy levels become discrete.

discovery.text: Smaller dots have larger band gaps — blue light. Larger dots have smaller gaps — red light. Size tunes the color.

twist.text: This only works at the nanoscale — a few nanometers larger and the quantum effect vanishes into bulk behavior.

climax.text: Samsung QLED TVs use quantum dots for vivid colors — each dot precisely sized for its spectral role.

punchline.text: Trap an electron in a tiny box and its color depends on the box size.

quiz.question: How do quantum dots produce different colors?
options: Different chemical compositions create different colors
Changing particle size alters the band gap, shifting emission wavelength
External electric fields change the dot's color
